newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia export coffee prices weak due to Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia export coffee prices weak due to Vietnam.

text.p: Indonesian local Robusta coffee prices were stable on Monday but export values were slightly weaker in the face of competition from Vietnam, traders said.

They said coffee was quoted unchanged from last week's 2,600-50 rupiah/kg in the key growing region of Lampung in South Sumatra, but export prices were weaker at $1,116-17/tonne fob Lampung compared with $1,200 a week ago.

The traders said monsoon rains recorded in many parts of the Indonesian archipelago had not affected the flowering process in South Sumatra, where the harvest ended in September, as the showers was sporadic and brief.

"If the rains are heavy and prolonged, there's a chance the flowers will drop off and affect the bean-forming process. But at the moment, the rains are actually good for the crop," one Lampung trader said.
Another trader said trading had been generally thin due to buyers being well covered and sellers holding back.
"There's about 75,000 to 80,000 tonnes of beans in the hands of farmers and local exporters and some of it is already committed," the trader said.
"The amount has to be carried over into next year for both exports and local consumption," he said.
He said there had also been pressure from Vietnam's relatively cheaper coffee, adding that Vietnamese coffee was heard done at $1,114/tonne fob Hanoi.
Another trader said one foreign-based exporter was heard buying about 100 tonnes/day last week in Lampung.
"Buying has generally been weak, expect for those who are covering positions," he added.
Traders said the first beans are expected to start forming in Lampung around March next year.
